steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: The goal entered is a 30% cut in grid electricity by 2030, with a $500,000 capital budget for 2027.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency alone is estimated to cut grid electricity use by about 6.2% to 17.6% of annual use. This does not reach the 30% goal by itself.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Whether solar can go on this roof cannot be answered yet. The roof is entered as pitched, so no array size or solar output has been estimated. Solar and battery scenarios were not costed and will be compared once the usable roof area is verified.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The building is flagged as a landmark in the city's records, so a Landmarks Preservation Commission review is needed before any rooftop or exterior work.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Jefferson Market Library (NYPL), 425 6 Avenue, Manhattan, built 1877, entered as 18,643 sq ft of floor area and a 7,020 sq ft pitched roof. Con Edison is the utility.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's building records show a 3-floor library built in 1877 with a landmark flag, one building on the lot, and a footprint of about 7,019 sq ft. A footprint is the ground area under the building, not a measured roof.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's energy report for 2024 shows 268,331 kWh (energy over time) of electricity, which matches the annual use entered. Site EUI (energy use per square foot) is 105 kBtu (thousand BTU) per sq ft.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The entered intake lists no existing solar, no other renewables and no efficiency work already done, so the plan assumes none exists. Please confirm. The goal baseline is the electricity bought from the grid.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A7: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: A9: Prices are planning-level benchmarks, not quotes. Efficiency costs $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved per year (standard package), from the middle half of completed NYC public-sector projects (NYSERDA data). The 10-20% savings are planning estimates, and only 62% to 88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share (NYC DCAS Local Law 87 annual report, fiscal year 2022).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The baseline is 268,331 kWh a year of grid electricity, as entered and matching the city's 2024 energy report. No existing solar lowers it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The building also burns natural gas, about 1,041,151 kBtu in 2024. Gas heating is outside an electricity-use goal, so it is not counted in the 30% target.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls) is estimated to save about 16,637 to 47,226 kWh a year. Only 62% to 88% of the predicted savings is counted, because the City's own audited projects delivered that share. Lighting type and building controls were not entered, so the confidence is low.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Confirm the current lighting type and controls before choosing measures, so that nothing already installed is paid for twice.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Solar was not sized. The roof is entered as pitched, and the sizing rules refuse flat-roof defaults for a pitched roof. This is a decision from the rules, not missing data. No array size, solar output or solar savings is given here.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Have an engineer or roofer verify the usable roof area (size, pitch, direction, structure, shading) and enter it in the intake, then re-plan. The 7,020 sq ft roof area is the entered figure and also needs to be verified. It is close to the city's 7,019 sq ft footprint.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness assessment lists this library as not solar ready, with the roof condition and roof age unknown. The roof should be checked, and possibly repaired or replaced, before solar.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Electricity price used for later savings is the New York commercial average of $0.1981 to $0.2418 per kWh, not this building's own tariff.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Scenario A (efficiency only): reduction of about 6.2% to 17.6% of annual use, which is 21% to 59% of the 30% goal. It does not reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A cost: typical range $47,092 to $161,804 upfront; the median of similar NYC projects is about $103,039. Net cost is the same, because no incentive is counted.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A simple payback is about 4.1 to 49.1 years (median case about 14 years), from annual savings of about $3,296 to $11,419. This is a simple payback, not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A budget strain: within budget, using about 9% to 32% of the $500,000. The estimated cost fits within the budget. It gives no backup power (0 outage hours).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The solar scenarios were not costed, because they depend on a verified usable roof area. Rooftop solar alone typically supplies only about 15-25% of use and would not reach 30% by itself. Meeting the goal may take more than the budget; that decision is yours after the gap is compared with savings.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The model treats the $500,000 capital budget as one total upfront amount.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Standard efficiency package: typical range $47,092 to $161,804; the median of similar NYC projects is about $103,039. Basis: about 40,250 kWh saved a year (middle of the 10-20% planning estimate) at $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved, from the middle half of completed NYC public-sector lighting and comprehensive projects (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Federal elective pay (direct payment of the solar credit to governmental entities) is listed as open, for solar placed in service by 2027-12-31. Whether this library's owner qualifies is not confirmed, and no solar is sized, so it is left out of net cost.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The NYSERDA NY-Sun commercial solar incentive could not be confirmed from an official page, so it is uncertain and left out of net cost. Check the NYSERDA dashboard in a browser before counting any incentive.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: NYC's sustainable roofs rules (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019) require a solar or green roof system on new buildings and on existing buildings undergoing certain major roof renovations. Ask the Department of Buildings whether a roof replacement here would trigger it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: No cost total includes replacing or repairing the roof. The roof age and condition are unknown and the city lists it as not solar ready, so a roofer's quote is needed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: gather recent bills, confirm the $500,000 capital budget for 2027, confirm the Con Edison tariff on a bill, and confirm the roof replacement year (not entered).
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a structural PE or RA analysis and a roof condition survey, including verifying the usable roof area, before any solar design.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: a standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls, after confirming what is already installed), which fits within the budget.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and Con Edison interconnection application: Landmarks Preservation Commission review, Department of Buildings permits, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, and the Con Edison interconnection application.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: only after the roof is verified, the landmarks review is cleared and a re-run plan shows the array size and cost.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: size any battery once critical load kW (how much power at one moment) and backup hours are entered, then check results against bills.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The critical loads entered are reading room cooling and lighting. Critical load kW and backup hours were not entered, so no battery was sized.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The efficiency-only scenario gives no backup power (0 outage hours). Solar panels without a battery shut off in an outage, and no battery option has been modeled yet.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: FEMA's current map shows flood zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) at this address, so no flood-zone review is triggered. Only the flood zone was read; heat and winter-storm ratings were not checked, nor the 2015 preliminary flood map.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A licensed structural PE or RA must analyze whether the roof can carry panels. The roof cannot be certified from these records. A roof condition survey is also required.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Landmarks Preservation Commission permit review is needed before any rooftop or exterior work, because the city record shows a landmark flag and the library sits in the Greenwich Village Historic District as you state. Whether the lot is parkland was not flagged in the city record.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, and a Con Edison utility interconnection review are required for any solar. The owner agency (NYPL) approval route should be confirmed. The list at the end of the plan has links to the offices.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates with ranges, not quotes, and savings cannot be guaranteed. A licensed PE or RA must analyze the roof structure.
roadmap.plain_answer: You asked whether the library can have rooftop solar and how to cut grid power 30% by 2030 on $500,000. Solar cannot be sized yet. The roof is pitched, and the planning rules do not allow solar to be sized on a pitched roof until an engineer or roofer verifies the usable area. This was a decision from those rules, not missing data. The building is also a city landmark, so a Landmarks Preservation Commission review is needed before any rooftop work, and the city's roof assessment lists the roof as not solar ready. An efficiency package alone is estimated to cut grid use by about 6% to 18% of your 268,331 kWh a year. That falls short of 30%, and it costs an estimated $47,092 to $161,804, well inside your budget. The plan assumes no existing solar or efficiency work. The gas heating is outside an electricity goal. Next steps: have an engineer or roofer verify the usable roof area, and start the landmarks and structural reviews. Then re-run the plan to compare solar and battery options against the 30% goal.
